Hi Samir—

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned:

- Goal: get a ballpark cost + configuration to hit your uptime and latency targets for the document-processing pipeline (real-time routing + on-demand summary).
- Your asks from the call:
  - Confirm expected monthly token volumes (you mentioned seasonal peaks).
  - Budget range target and acceptable $/1M-tokens economics.
  - Any hard latency SLOs per request (p95).

Initial Redwood hypotheses we want to validate:
- Workload is continuous with modest burstiness (20–30% peaks). Continuous batching will be effective if per-request average tokens > 400 and inter-arrival times < ~120ms.
- A routing profile with a primary low-latency tier + fallback higher-batch tier should meet your uptime goals while improving unit economics.

What we need from you (small ask):
1) Traffic sample (CSV) with timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_id for a 48–72 hour window.
2) Target budget range (monthly) or target $/1M tokens you would consider for an initial pilot.
3) Any blocking security/procurement constraints.

If you prefer, reply with the sample attached and a one-line budget. We’ll run a quick costing with two scenarios (low-latency prioritized; cost-optimized with batching) and return an SLO-aware $/1M estimate.

Thanks—Marissa will shadow the costing; Aditya will validate batching assumptions.

—Neha

Neha / Aditya —

Thanks for the forward and the sample, Samir. Quick summary of our early estimate and assumptions (short form):

Scenario A — Low-latency primary
- Concurrency target: 70 qps sustained at peak (buffering for 10% headroom)
- Batching profile: conservative batching (window 50–80ms), avg effective requests per batch ~2.6
- Effective tokens/request (after prefix reuse & KV hints): 520 in -> ~470 net
- Estimated unit: ~$1,350 per 1M tokens
- Expected p95: ~230–270ms depending on model variant and region routing

Scenario B — Cost-optimized with continuous batching
- Concurrency target: 60 qps sustained (burst capacity available)
- Batching profile: continuous batching with small window (200–300ms), avg effective requests per batch ~6.8
- Effective tokens/request: 520 in -> ~410 net (KV/prefix caching applied)
- Estimated unit: ~$920 per 1M tokens (approx aligns to their $800–$1,200 target)
- Expected p95: ~350–450ms (tradeoff for cost)

Assumptions & notes:
- These numbers assume use of a quantized model variant (FP16->4-bit path) for cost scenario B; model selection could move unit economics by ±15%.
- Continuous batching effectiveness hinges on request inter-arrival distribution — sample looks favorable (avg inter-arrival below 120ms at peak).
- SOC2 + procurement gating: procurement wants vendor SOC2 report and standard redwood SOW + SLA. Ops email included.

Deliverables attached: redwood-estimate-finnect.xlsx (breakdown by token bands, instance sizing, expected monthly spend) and batching-assumptions-brief.pdf (one-page summary of windows and concurrency guidance).

Next steps:
1) We send the two-scenario write-up to Samir tomorrow AM with the XLS.
2) If Finnect wants to pursue pilot, spin up a short A/B canary: 2 weeks, controlled traffic, specific eval prompts.

If you want any adjustments before we send, tell me by 09:30 AM tomorrow.

—Marissa
